the As contamination of this aquifer was caused by the dissolution of calcium-containing As species, and the subsequent retention of As in the aquifer by precipitation of calcium arsenate.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
arsenate retention by calcium-rich sediments is a common mechanism that should be considered for As mobility and transport studies.
the presence of calcium in a solid form (e.g., calcium arsenates) can be used to control As mobility.
the disposal of residues from mining operations, which are rich in calcium arsenates, can be a source of long-term contamination of the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium arsenates are a major contributor to the arsenic problem in Mexico and other parts of the world where mining has occurred.

the dissolution of solid calcium arsenates is a widespread mechanism of As mobilisation that can be triggered by the availability of calcium ions, and that the precipitation of calcium arsenate species can be a mechanism of As retention in calcareous environments.

calcium arsenates, such as the ones reported here, should be considered in the environmental geochemical models of As mobility in calcium-rich systems, especially those where iron(III) minerals are scarce.
